stem: Pressure sensors along the small intestine record contractions during a fasting study. A motilin stimulus is followed by a coordinated sequence that travels along the intestine. Which of the following observations best identifies the resulting motility pattern?

options.label: A
options.text: Repeated local mixing keeps the contents within one short segment
options.explanation: Local mixing without net propulsion describes segmentation. It does not match the coordinated migrating response to motilin.
options.misconception: Substitutes stationary segmentation for the migrating motility response.

options.label: B
options.text: A migrating contraction complex moves contents along the intestine
options.explanation: Motilin stimulates a migrating motility complex. A traveling sequence distinguishes this response from stationary mixing contractions.
options.misconception: No misconception: motilin supports a propagating migrating contraction complex.

options.label: C
options.text: A stationary contraction blocks movement throughout the intestine
options.explanation: A persistent stationary block is not a migrating complex and would not explain the sequential pressure changes.
options.misconception: Mistakes a traveling contraction sequence for a stationary obstruction.

options.label: D
options.text: A fall in all contractions increases contact with the mucosal surface
options.explanation: Reduced contractile activity is the opposite of the observed coordinated contraction sequence. It does not establish enhanced mixing.
options.misconception: Reverses the observed contractile response and assumes improved mixing.

options.label: E
options.text: Simultaneous opposing contractions prevent any forward movement
options.explanation: Opposing local contractions can mix contents, but the recorded pattern propagates along the intestine rather than remaining stationary.
options.misconception: Confuses local opposing contractions with a forward-propagating pattern.

context:
Learning objective: Identify intestinal motor patterns from their spatial sequence. Motilin is associated with a migrating complex; segmentation primarily mixes chyme without net propulsion.

Motilin stimulates a migrating motility complex. A traveling sequence distinguishes this response from stationary mixing contractions.
